editorial.headline: Plumbing Work Where Water Systems Meet Building Reality
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers the installation and upkeep of essential water, wastewater and drainage systems across residential and non-residential buildings.
editorial.body:
Plumbing is not a finishing detail; it is the working infrastructure that allows a building to receive clean water, manage wastewater and drain reliably. This activity covers installing, repairing and maintaining clean-water, wastewater and drainage lines, together with sanitary equipment, in both residential and non-residential buildings. Its practical scope includes water lines, clean-water distribution pipes, dirty-water pipes, and installations for water-treatment plants or reverse-osmosis systems.

The breadth matters because the work follows a system through its operating life. Installation is only one part of the activity: repair and maintenance are expressly within scope as well. That makes this a building-services activity concerned with the condition and continuity of plumbing systems, rather than simply the initial placement of pipes or fittings. The inclusion of sanitary equipment and water-treatment installations also reflects how closely water distribution, treatment and disposal are connected within a building.

Registration is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales. Nationally, the activity is TERBUKA to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. That is the national position stated in the record: foreign participation is not capped below full ownership for this activity.

Bali presents no moratorium block for PMA registration here. The province permanently blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk activities, but this activity is recorded as not blocked: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. In practical terms, the national openness remains meaningful in Bali for this activity; the Bali record does not add a separate foreign-ownership cap or partnership condition.
